items.text: – Viiiž, Baba, Baba, kupiš mi ovu vejiku lutkicu?
items.q: On the street, a stranger's little girl asks her dad for a big doll. Does it sound like baby talk?
before: …lampu koja je uništila onu ugodnu, umirujuću tamnu tišinu, a nije davala dovoljno svjetla da me negdje povede. Lampu koja trepće u ruci djevojke za boju čijih vrata nikad nisam znao na kojem je mjestu u kutiji drvenih bojica. Jedna djevojčica dolazi bučno i staje pored mene. Gleda igračke. Kaže:

items.text: Čovjeka uhvati govnovrtoglavica. Što više razmišljaš o tome, sve te jače hvata govnovrtoglavica.
items.q: A student describes a Magritte painting; 'govnovrtoglavica' is her crude made-up blend of shit and dizziness. Does it work?
before: – ... Gledajte koliko je zaista poticajno za razmišljanje. Nacrtao je ovo i ispod napisao: ovo nije lula.

items.text: I ti, s tim svojim kurčevitim načinom govora, trebao si se zvati Alain Kurčon.
items.q: 'Alain Kurčon' is meant as a rude pun on the actor Alain Delon. Would Croatian readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?

items.text: – To je mramal. Mramal znači jako skupo.
items.q: A small boy says 'mramal' for 'mramor' and wrongly thinks it means expensive; both mistakes are intended. Does it sound like a child?
before: Krenuli smo dalje. Na pola puta bila je kuća. Njezin zid je bio lijep. Ghassem bi uvijek govorio:

items.text: Kiša ne pada uvis sa zemlje.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Ruka mi je kratka, a sjedinjenje s tobom daleko.
items.q: Amir tells the girl he loves why he holds back. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Ne jedi tugu, moj pametni dječače.
items.q: Maman comforts her little boy, whose feet are hurt. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Bibi, neka joj je laka zemlja, znala je reći u ovakvim trenucima: Ako kažem, gori mi jezik; ako ne kažem, gori mi srž kostiju.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Kaže: "Dobra se godina od proljeća poznaje."
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: "Ono vino što je onde istina je ne metafora."
items.q: Hafez's line, read one way: the wine is real, not a metaphor. Read another: not real, only a metaphor. Do both readings work here?

items.text: S ove strane odmotavam nit riječi, a s druge strane ti skupljaš riječi.
items.q: The author unravels a thread of words; the reader gathers them. Does this read naturally?
